section_summary: This section concerns Japanese exchange controls and the difficulty American citizens and firms faced in converting or remitting funds from Japan. It includes cases involving estates, company sales, insurance assets and Kodak Japan, along with State Department discussions of possible reciprocal releases of blocked funds. Related records cover traveler drafts, evacuation advice, Indochinese bank accounts and British negotiations with Japan.

subfiles.title: Suggested instructions for American property inventories
subfiles.about: Proposes guidance for Americans documenting property they might lose in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum specifies inventory categories, valuations in local and American currency, evidence of ownership and value, and sworn copies for Embassy files. It cautions that submitting an inventory guarantees neither acceptance nor government responsibility.

subfiles.title: Advice to Americans to leave disturbed Far Eastern areas
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Tokyo; repeated to Peiping, Chungking, and Hong Kong
subfiles.about: Directs officers to discreetly suggest withdrawal to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites worsening conditions across China, Japan, Hong Kong and French Indochina. It especially urges women, children and men whose presence is not essential to use available transport, and requests estimates of likely departures.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies’ position on Sakuma operations
subfiles.about: Says the company can continue operating while Japanese orders and material permits remain in force.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald attributes pressure to sell to denial of a dollar exchange permit.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank’s new policy on drafts for U.S. travelers
subfiles.about: Reports that the bank now issues yen drafts rather than fixed dollar drafts.
subfiles.summary: Travelers could carry the equivalent of up to 500 yen. The bank’s new drafts would be converted at its buying rate when presented in the United States, exposing travelers to exchange changes.

subfiles.title: Mary Bell’s refused estate remittance permit
subfiles.about: Reports denial of a permit to remit 15,000 yen from the Worden estate.
subfiles.summary: Grew anticipates more such cases as Americans liquidate property before leaving Japan.

subfiles.title: Note on review of a telegram
subfiles.about: Records review and approval of a telegram’s form.
subfiles.summary: A handwritten note says the telegram was considered and initialled.

subfiles.title: Orvis Brothers’ request for help collecting the Itoh debt
subfiles.from: F. Howard Smith, Orvis Brothers & Co.
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a message seeking a remittance permit for Takenosuke Itoh’s debt.
subfiles.summary: The firm says $36,979.21 remains unpaid because Japanese exchange permits have been denied. It has attached New York assets and offers to lift the attachments after partial payment and a plan for the balance.

subfiles.title: Orvis Brothers’ message to Williams
subfiles.from: Department of State, forwarding Orvis Brothers & Co.
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Tokyo, for Frank S. Williams
subfiles.about: Forwards the firm’s request for assistance obtaining Itoh’s remittance permit.
subfiles.summary: The telegram repeats the debt, attached assets and proposed partial settlement.

subfiles.title: Grew’s approach on Mary Bell’s permit
subfiles.about: Reports informal oral representations to Japan’s foreign minister concerning Mary Bell.
subfiles.summary: Grew raised Bell’s refused exchange permit on November 10.

subfiles.title: Instruction to protest restrictions on American remittances
subfiles.about: Suggests an approach to Japan’s Foreign Office about exchange permits.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Japan to permit prompt remittance of proceeds from American liquidations. It objects particularly to pressure to sell American interests without a permit to transfer the proceeds.

subfiles.title: Grew reports protest on exchange permits
subfiles.about: Reports carrying out instructions with Japan’s foreign minister.
subfiles.summary: The minister promised an immediate investigation.

subfiles.title: Japanese businesses seeking Seattle bank loans
subfiles.about: Relays confidential information about Japanese business houses in Seattle.
subfiles.summary: Hoover says they have quietly sought bank loans after previously maintaining substantial balances.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies request continued Sakuma supplies
subfiles.about: Asks the Embassy to seek continued orders and supplies for Sakuma.
subfiles.summary: The company would sell its holding if payment could be made in U.S. dollars.

subfiles.title: Proposal to exchange Embassy dollars for Sakuma yen
subfiles.about: Asks whether Embassy operating funds could be exchanged for the company’s yen.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald seeks a way to convert proceeds from the proposed sale.

subfiles.title: Reply to Paraffine Companies on exchange difficulties
subfiles.about: Explains State’s action on remittance permits and rejects use of Embassy funds.
subfiles.summary: Grady says the Embassy is being instructed to approach the Foreign Office. Government expenditures abroad are too small to meet requests to exchange blocked private funds, and choosing beneficiaries would raise priority questions.

subfiles.title: Correspondence on the Sakuma Company
subfiles.about: Forwards Paraffine Companies correspondence for the ambassador’s information.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure list identifies two company letters and Grady’s reply.

subfiles.title: Sale of Japanese currency in the United States
subfiles.about: Assesses an advertisement offering yen below Japan’s official rate.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum compares official and open market yen rates and notes that taking currency into Japan requires a permit. It sees little reason for Securities and Exchange Commission action unless a law has been violated.

subfiles.title: Berle’s inquiry about a yen advertisement
subfiles.about: Requests advice about an advertisement selling Japanese currency.
subfiles.summary: Berle forwards the Securities and Exchange Commission’s question.

subfiles.title: Telephone response to Goodfellow
subfiles.about: Records the Department’s refusal to assist Goodfellow’s proposed funds transaction.
subfiles.summary: Mackay told Goodfellow the proposed arrangement was a private matter.

subfiles.title: Handwritten comment on Goodfellow recommendation
subfiles.about: Records an internal handwritten response to a recommendation.
subfiles.summary: The partly illegible note appears to concur with the recommendation.

subfiles.title: Conversation on releasing funds blocked by Japanese exchange control
subfiles.about: Discusses Goodfellow’s proposed exchange of blocked American claims for Japanese insurance assets.
subfiles.summary: Goodfellow proposed matching future payments owed to former American owners of Oriental Consolidated Mining Company with Japanese insurers’ assets in the United States. Officials doubted Japan would accept and noted that helping this particular private arrangement could disadvantage other Americans with blocked funds.

subfiles.title: Status of the Paraffine Companies case
subfiles.about: Reviews Embassy action and the company’s changing position on a Sakuma sale.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy had raised dollar exchange permits informally, while Sakuma continued receiving orders and supplies. The memorandum finds no need for new instructions until the company decides whether to sell.

subfiles.title: Handwritten instruction concerning December correspondence
subfiles.about: Requests a draft response concerning recent correspondence.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten instruction is partly illegible.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies report threatened loss of Army orders
subfiles.about: Warns that Sakuma may lose orders and supplies after the end of 1940.
subfiles.summary: Shainwald says the firm is being singled out for pressure to eliminate foreign capital. It refuses payment in yen and asks the Embassy to pursue a dollar exchange permit.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Paraffine Companies letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s further information on Sakuma.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it is forwarding the information to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: December Paraffine Companies letter forwarded to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Shainwald’s December 6 letter.
subfiles.summary: The letter concerns Sakuma’s treatment by Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Bank of Indochina account restrictions
subfiles.about: Responds to claims that U.S. financial controls forced Indochina into a yen bloc.
subfiles.summary: After consulting Treasury, the Department describes available transfers and licenses and disputes the bank inspector’s general complaint. It asks the consul to present the information to bank and government officials.

subfiles.title: Bank of Indochina cites blocked dollar receipts
subfiles.about: Reports two payments the bank says entered blocked accounts.
subfiles.summary: The cases concern freight for the Bougainville and a letter of credit for zinc exports. The inspector general argues the bank needs usable dollar receipts for American business.

subfiles.title: Request for Treasury advice on Indochina bank complaint
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks Treasury suggestions for replying to Hanoi’s latest telegram.
subfiles.summary: The letter reviews the earlier response on transfers into the bank’s U.S. accounts and encloses the consul’s December 30 telegram. Page 129 is a duplicate or retained copy of its closing page.

subfiles.title: Exchange difficulties of Mary C. Bell
subfiles.about: Transmits records of Grew’s representations on Bell’s exchange permit.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses a conversation memorandum and the oral statement left with Japan’s foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Grew’s conversation with Matsuoka on Bell’s permit
subfiles.about: Records informal representations about Bell’s refused permit.
subfiles.summary: Bell sought foreign exchange equivalent to 15,000 yen.

subfiles.title: Oral statement concerning Mary Bell’s estate proceeds
subfiles.about: Sets out Bell’s request to remit her father’s estate proceeds to heirs in the United States.
subfiles.summary: The Finance Ministry refused Bell’s October 15 application on October 25.

subfiles.title: Record-only file note
subfiles.about: Marks an item for the record.
subfiles.summary: The short handwritten note is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Exchange permits for liquidation of American interests
subfiles.about: Transmits records of Grew’s November 30 approach to Japan’s foreign minister.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses a conversation memorandum and an oral statement.

subfiles.title: Grew’s conversation with Matsuoka on American funds
subfiles.about: Records Grew’s request that Japan address obstacles to American remittances.
subfiles.summary: Matsuoka said he would investigate immediately.

subfiles.title: Oral protest on liquidation proceeds
subfiles.about: Urges permits for Americans to transfer funds from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The statement objects to pressure on American firms to sell interests when permits to remit sale proceeds are withheld.

subfiles.title: Confidential-file reference
subfiles.about: Indicates filing of a related item in confidential files.
subfiles.summary: The page contains no substantive document text.

subfiles.title: Freezing of Japanese funds
subfiles.about: Introduces confidential information concerning a freeze of Japanese funds.
subfiles.summary: Only a fragment of the memorandum’s substantive text is legible.

subfiles.title: Japanese funds deposited in Brazil
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Yokohama Specie Bank instructions concerning deposits in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The original is filed under 832.5151/1604.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank–Java Bank agreement
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram reporting terms of a monetary traffic agreement.
subfiles.summary: The agreement concerns the Netherlands Indies.

subfiles.title: Currency allowance for Monterey passengers
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on currency Americans could take from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Monterey passengers could carry the equivalent of 500 yen.

subfiles.title: Proposed tobacco purchase financed by Japanese securities
subfiles.about: Points to a letter proposing a government loan secured by Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: The financing would support a tobacco sale to Japan through Mitsui.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply on Indochina bank transactions
subfiles.about: Explains why two Indochina-related payments were blocked or could be released.
subfiles.summary: Treasury attributes the freight payment’s blocking to inadequate source information and says zinc proceeds could enter the bank’s free account under its license.

subfiles.title: Kodak Japan requests assistance with exchange permits
subfiles.about: Requests instructions after Kodak Japan reports repeated denial of remittance permits.
subfiles.summary: Kodak Japan holds substantial cash but cannot remit profits, pay for imported merchandise or repay advances from its American parent. Grew forwards the company’s figures and suggests that Eastman Kodak also present the case to the Department.

subfiles.title: Kodak Japan accounts and rejected applications
subfiles.about: Details cash, unpaid obligations and applications for exchange permits.
subfiles.summary: The statement reports ¥736,121.03 cash on hand and ¥720,169.07 in unremitted profits and sums owed to Eastman Kodak. It lists rejected applications for profits, merchandise payments and miscellaneous debits, with an account of the Finance Ministry discouraging further applications.

subfiles.title: Instructions on Kodak Japan’s blocked funds
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to pursue appropriate measures for releasing Kodak Japan’s funds.
subfiles.summary: The Department refers Grew to standing instructions and comparable cases.

subfiles.title: Possible reciprocal release of Japanese and American funds
subfiles.about: Assesses whether a British-style reciprocal funds release could work for the United States.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues Japan would have little reason to negotiate while Japanese assets move freely in the United States. Freezing them might give the United States bargaining power, but Japan would likely regard that action as economic pressure.

subfiles.title: Summary of British proposal to release blocked funds
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Tokyo despatch on proposed reciprocal release of British and Japanese funds.
subfiles.summary: The proposal could help British subjects leave Japan and might set a precedent.

subfiles.title: Move to effect release of British funds in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports British negotiations to exchange blocked funds with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The British Embassy says Japan received its reciprocal release proposal favorably and both sides are estimating affected funds. The arrangement could let British subjects leave Japan; Grew notes it might become a precedent for American policy.

subfiles.title: Japanese ordinance on assets frozen abroad
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese requirement to disclose assets frozen abroad.
subfiles.summary: Grew interprets the ordinance as preparation for diplomatic negotiations to repatriate or exchange frozen assets. He argues that reciprocity offers better protection for American interests than relying on treatment Japan grants another country.
